messages:
Priya Patel: Thanks for joining todays all-hands. Starting a short follow-up thread for process questions we didnt finish: release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs. Keep questions concise and well reply live in ~20m.

Alex Chen: Are weekly release trains still the default for hosted? noticed a few recent slips.

Priya Patel: Yes  weekly remains the default for hosted API. Slips were due to infra migrations and a couple of emergency rollbacks. Were documenting an "exceptions" policy (infra migrations, major DB ops, security hotfix weeks) that teams must announce 7d prior.

Samir Gupta: Canary/rollback specifics? also, do runtime-impacting PRs need full perf suite before merge or is smoke OK?

Priya Patel: Canary: default 30m at ~5% traffic, expand to 25% then full if green. Rollback triggers: error-rate >0.5% absolute above baseline OR p95 latency +15% sustained >5m OR dependency error spikes. Runtime PRs require smoke perf checks pre-merge; the full perf suite runs post-merge and blocks promotion to broad pools if it flags regressions. Use the "perf-smoke" PR label.

Marta Lopez: Oncall: any plan to move infra to 2-week rotations? 1-week is burning people out.

Priya Patel: Were piloting 2-week rotations for infra/SRE next quarter with paid handover overlap and a documented shadowing flow. Runtime/product teams will stay 1-week for now. Coverage model: runtime = 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra = 1 primary + 2 secondaries.

Alex Chen: Will Releases UI show route-level canary health (p50/p95/error-rate) or just service-level?

Priya Patel: Console will show per-route p50/p95/error-rate and a canary-health badge in Releases. UX will add an explanation tooltip and per-route mini-charts. Alex: please mock and link the figma in the follow-up doc.

Samir Gupta: Quality bars: are we mandating repo-level coverage %? Folks worried about a hard number.

Priya Patel: No single org-wide coverage number. Baseline = CI green + unit tests for new code. Recommended targets: libs >=60%, customer-facing/runtime services >=80%. We'll add repo README expectations and a short PR checklist (lint, types, unit tests, perf-smoke if runtime). If below target, require a testing rationale in the PR.

Marta Lopez: SLAs: public hosted still 99.9? higher tiers for Dedicated?

Priya Patel: Public hosted SLA target remains 99.9. Dedicated customers can opt into 99.95 SLA for reserved capacity under contract. Credits are prorated per the contract window; Legal is finalizing wording. We'll publish an SLA matrix with worked examples next week.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-07-18 (build: 2026.07.18-f3b9).

Alex Chen: Action items? owners?

Priya Patel: Action items: (1) Ill draft a 1-page FAQ + exceptions policy (owner: Priya) by EOD Friday. (2) Marta to write hosted vs dedicated release differences (owner: Marta). (3) Alex to mock console canary/route-health UI (owner: Alex). (4) Samir to propose PR template update with perf-smoke entry (owner: Samir). We'll post PRs to #eng-docs and iterate.

Marta Lopez: I'll open the draft PR by EOD tomorrow.

Samir Gupta: I'll sketch the PR template and add the perf-smoke snippet.

Priya Patel: Thanks all  we'll answer live Qs at 2pm PT and post the recording + notes after. :thumbsup:
